summary.headline: Supriya Lifescience Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell 37.5% to INR45 crore (22% margin) on LATAM regulatory shock, Ambernath costs; FY27 margin guidance cut to 23-25%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 3.2% YoY to INR206 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR45 crore from INR73 crore and PAT to INR29 crore from INR50 crore. Management attributed the margin drop to LATAM regulatory changes that made high-margin products controlled substances, Ambernath ramp-up costs (about INR60 crore for FY27 with little revenue), and higher raw material and solvent prices. EBITDA margin guidance was cut to 23-25% from the earlier range, while the INR1,000 crore revenue target for FY27 was reaffirmed. The Ambernath EU audit was scheduled for the week of the call, and a large CDMO contract was said to be close to signing.

segments.name: Exports (geography)
segments.commentary: Exports were 80% of Q2 FY27 revenue: Europe 43%, Asia 36%, LATAM 12%. LATAM share was up to 21% in an earlier period before falling back to 12%.

segments.name: Ambernath facility
segments.commentary: Ramping up; about INR60 crore of expenses expected in FY27 with near-zero revenue this year. Designed for INR450-500 crore revenue once EU approval is in place; breakeven seen at INR160-200 crore revenue.

segments.name: New launches
segments.commentary: Two anesthetic liquid inhalation products launched in Q2 FY27 from Ambernath; two ADHD products in pipeline. Traction is mainly in semi-regulated markets with lower ASPs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance revised down to 23-25%; management said it expects about 25% for the full year, with upside possible if raw material and solvent costs ease.

FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,000 crore reaffirmed; management said it is very confident, citing an order book and about INR265 crore of inventory. H1 revenue was INR396 crore, implying about INR600 crore needed in H2.
Medium-term revenue growth guidance of 20%+ per year for the next 3-4 years, driven by baseline business, new launches and CDMO deals.
Margin normalisation is expected in FY28 once Ambernath is approved and LATAM sales resume. Management declined to give FY28 margin guidance and will revisit after the EU approval.
Management said LATAM import permits could take 4-5 months, so the margin impact is expected to persist for the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Q2 FY27 capex of INR18.8 crore and H1 FY27 capex of INR35.4 crore, mainly for Ambernath plus maintenance, the Ribo block and formulation plant.

Ambernath EU audit scheduled for the week of the call (November 2026); approval is a precondition for meaningful revenue. Product registrations could take about 1-1.5 years after approval to reach meaningful scale.
Module E API capacity can take the liquid anesthetic product to about 1,100 tonnes, with customer scale-up expected over 4-5 years.
Contrast media product said to be close to launch, with commercial-scale plant scale-up expected by next quarter.
demand_pricing: Margin decomposition by management: typical margin 34-35%, current about 22%. The 11-12 point gap is roughly 6 points from Ambernath costs, 3 points from LATAM regulatory and mix change, and 3 points from raw material and solvent inflation.

LATAM markets (Colombia, Peru, Uruguay and others) reclassified high-margin products as controlled substances with immediate effect and no stock window. Customers now need import authorisations, which management expects to take 4-5 months.

Raw material and solvent prices kept rising after Q1 because of geopolitical tensions. Contracts with larger customers were priced at older rates, so the price pass-through is expected to flow through over the next 2 quarters.
Statins intermediate: mid-level monthly volumes; the company is the only fully integrated Indian producer and competes with China on price.
ADHD API market estimated at USD100-150 million; a long-term supply contract with a US company is at an early stage. Regulatory approvals are expected in 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is hit by the LATAM regulatory change, and is the impact permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it transient, lasting a few quarters, while import authorisations are pending. It cited 4-5 months for customers to obtain permits; the change took effect immediately with no stock-up window across 3-4 countries.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the INR1,000 crore FY27 revenue target given H1 of INR396 crore and about INR265 crore of inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very confident, citing the order book, and expects the new products in semi-regulated markets plus the anesthetic CMO deal to offset LATAM.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin decline split, and why is it larger than peers' given backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Split: about 6 points Ambernath, 3 points LATAM and mix, 3 points raw material and solvent. The CFO attributed the solvent and raw material pressure to crude-derived basic chemicals and drum versus ISO tank pricing, plus customer pushback on price increases.

qa_highlights.question: When does Ambernath break even and what revenue is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the breakeven sweet spot is INR160-200 crore of revenue, versus about INR60 crore of expenses now. Meaningful scale is expected 1-1.5 years after EU approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide FY28 margin, saying it will come back after EU approval and the next couple of quarters. It said normalisation is expected once Ambernath and LATAM contribute.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a communication gap, given the margin guidance was held in the prior call?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the feedback and said the LATAM regulatory change happened after the Q1 call, so the lost POs could not have been pre-empted.

risks_watch: Ambernath EU audit outcome (week of the call) and timing of product approvals; any delay pushes back revenue and breakeven.
LATAM import authorisations: customers need 4-5 months, so the high-margin volume recovery is uncertain for the next two quarters.
H2 revenue must be about INR600 crore to hit INR1,000 crore; H1 was INR396 crore and inventory is about INR265 crore.
Raw material and solvent price pass-through: management expects the impact to show in the next 2 quarters, and some large pharma customers are resisting price hikes.
Large CDMO contract (anesthetic, API-led) is close to signing but not yet announced; approvals in multiple markets are needed for the formulation phase.
Management has not guided FY28 margin, and investors questioned communication after the Q1 call; further clarity is expected in the next couple of quarters.
summary.management_tone: Defensive on the margin cut, though confident on revenue. Management attributed the miss to a sudden LATAM regulatory change, Ambernath delays and raw material inflation, and repeatedly called the margin drop transient. It declined to guide FY28 margins and acknowledged communication concerns from investors.
key_quotes: So, we are looking at about 25% for the remaining part of FY '27. So, for the full year, it would be around 25%.
We are very confident that we will be able to achieve our guidance of INR1,000 crores.
So, I think once these 3 things are in place, they would drive the growth moving forward.
At this point, we are not guiding for the next financial year.
